stem.text: Use the limit comparison test with \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{3}} \) to determine whether the series \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n \), where \( a_n = \frac{2 n^{2} + 2}{6 n^{5} + 9} \), converges or diverges. State the conclusion, naming the series it concerns.

answer_key.label: \( \sum a_n \) converges, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{a_n}{1/n^{3}} = \frac{1}{3} \) is positive and finite and \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{3}} \) converges.

worked_solution.text: Compare the series \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n \) with \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{3}} \), the p-series with \( p = 3 \), since the degrees of the denominator and numerator of the terms differ by 3. Both have positive terms.
The limit \( \frac{1}{3} \) is positive and finite, and \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{3}} \) converges because \( p = 3 > 1 \).
\( \sum a_n \) converges, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{a_n}{1/n^{3}} = \frac{1}{3} \) is positive and finite and \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{3}} \) converges.
